messages:
anya: quick sync — i'm trying to land a change to the dedicated GPU pool autoscaler. current autoscaler uses token throughput + avg latency to decide scale, but we've been seeing tail-p95 spikes that break SLOs for interactive tenants. i sketched a small alternative that reacts to tail latency signals and prewarm credits instead of raw qps. thoughts?

leo: +1 this matches what we saw in canary. throughput drops but p95 spikes when cache misses or kv-evictions happen. reactive qps scaling is too slow.

pranav: can you paste the sketch? curious how you avoid oscillation if p95 is noisy.

anya: sure — rough policy DSL:```yaml
scale_policy:
  mode: latency_tail
  metric: request_latency_p95_ms
  target: 120        # ms p95 per tenant
  cooldown: 45s
  buffer: 0.15       # fraction of pool headroom reserved for spikes
  prewarm_credit: 2  # warm GPUs to keep for burst
  fallback: throughput  # degrade to qps-based if telemetry missing
```
Key ideas: 1) use aggregated p95 per tenant over sliding 60s window, 2) keep a small elastic prewarm credit that the allocator holds as <soft> leases, 3) if KV cache miss rate > 0.1 then increase prewarm multiplier, 4) operator exposes admit token to control-plane so we can charge and observe.

maria: i like the prewarm_credit idea. question: who owns the prewarm lifecycle? operator or control-plane? i want the operator to be dumb (start/stop nodes) and control-plane to be decision-maker, but we need an admission surface to signal warm vs cold.

leo: that's the boundary we debated before. operationally i prefer operator owns the low-level lifecycle (provision, drain, health), control-plane owns "intent" (desired warm count, headroom). operator exposes an API: SetHeadroom(tenant, count, ttl). operator keeps soft prewarmed GPUs until ttl or used.

pranav: agree. that keeps operator simple. one implementation detail: operator should expose both strong and soft reservations so we can do graceful eviction. also need jitter/randomized backoff when multiple tenants spike concurrently.

anya: good call on soft vs strong. sketching admission: control-plane asks operator for N soft slots for tenant T. operator returns token IDs. control-plane attaches token to requests to prefer routing to soft prewarms. if token reused beyond threshold treat as hot and convert to strong reservation.

infra-bot: deploy/rollout: canary group = dedicated pools in us-west-2 only, feature flag = "p95-driven-autoscale". alerting: p95 > 130ms for 2min => rollback.

maria: two tradeoffs to call out: 1) telemetry fidelity — p95 needs consistent aggregation boundary (client vs proxy vs runtime). we must pick one. 2) cost accounting — prewarm credits must be billable or at least metered per tenant to avoid freebies.

dave: about telemetry: prefer runtime-side p95 measured after kv cache layer (so it captures misses). proxies add noise from network. also suggest exposing a p99 for emergency guardrail but not to drive routine scale.

leo: oscillation mitigation: implement a hysteresis window and smoothing: only scale-up immediately for sustained p95 breach >2 samples, scale-down after 3x cooldowns. Also cap scale rate to +20% nodes per minute.

pranav: + put a fallback: if telemetry stream drops (kafka lag >30s), policy should revert to throughput mode. also record a decision event for offline analysis.

anya: next steps i propose: 1) write an RFC that defines operator-control-plane API: SetHeadroom, ListTokens, ClaimToken, ConvertToken, ReleaseToken, 2) proto + small shim in operator to accept headroom intent (v1: soft only), 3) controlled canary with infra-bot plan. i'll draft RFC and volunteer to own prototype. anyone want to co-own the RFC?

leo: i'll pair on the proto and operator shim.

maria: i'll own the telemetry spec (p95 definition, tag semantics, sampling).

pranav: i'll help with the autoscaler logic and the smoothing heuristics.

anya: awesome — i'll open the RFC PR later today and link to this thread. /cc @everyone :thumbsup:
